en: The Sūtra of the Holy Mother Prajñāpāramitā Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta, Court Attendant of the Great Tang, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Grand Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Purple-Robed Subject, by imperial decree.
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Blessed One was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain near the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the samādhi called "Proclaiming the True Dharma through Profound Radiance.

At that moment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara was present in the assembly of the Buddha; this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva had already been able to practice the profound Prajñāpāramitā and perceived that the intrinsic nature of the five aggregates is entirely empty.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, approached Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Mahāsattva and said:
“If a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to practice and study this profound Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā, how should they study it?”
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:
"Listen attentively now; I shall proclaim it for you."

If any son or daughter of good family wishes to practice and study this profound Dharma-gate of the *prajñāpāramitā*, they should contemplate that the intrinsic nature of the five aggregates is entirely empty.
What is meant by the self-nature emptiness of the five aggregates?
It is said that form itself is emptiness, and emptiness itself is form;
form is not different from emptiness, and emptiness is not different from form.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are likewise so.
"Śāriputra, all these phenomena have such a characteristic of emptiness: they are neither produced nor extinguished; they are neither defiled nor pure; they neither increase nor decrease."
Śāriputra! Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no feeling, perception, mental formations, or consciousness;
there is no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind.
There is no form, sound, odor, taste, touch, or mental object;
there is no eye-element and no eye-consciousness-element, and so on, up to no mind-element and no mind-consciousness-element;
there is no ignorance and no extinction of ignorance, and so on, up to no old age and death, nor the extinction of old age and death.
There is no suffering, no origin, no cessation, and no path;
there is no wisdom, nothing to be attained, and likewise nothing that is not attained. "Śāriputra!
Because there is nothing to be attained, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, by practicing in accordance with the Prajñāpāramitā, has no attachment and no hindrance in his mind;
because he is without attachment and without hindrance, he is free from fear, far removed from all inverted delusions, and reaches ultimate parinirvāṇa.
All Buddhas of the three periods of time, by relying upon this Prajñāpāramitā, have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Therefore, one should know that the Prajñāpāramitā is a vast illumination, an unsurpassed illumination, and an unequaled illumination; it can extinguish all suffering and affliction. It is the true and non-deceptive Dharma, which those who practice and study should learn in this way.
I shall now proclaim the great vidyā-mantra of the Prajñāpāramitā, which says: *Tadyathā | oṃ gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā*. Śāriputra!
If any bodhisattva-mahāsattvas can recite these mantra-words of the Prajñāpāramitā, they are thereby training in the profound Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, the World-Honored One arose calmly from samādhi and praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Good son! It is as you have said; it is so, it is so!
The *prajñāpāramitā* should be studied in this very way; this is the true, supreme, and ultimate [teaching], which all Tathāgatas likewise rejoice in."

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, together with all the bhikṣus, and the entire great assembly—including the devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others of the world—having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Perfection of Wisdom, the Holy Mother of the Buddhas, Spoken by the Buddha.
